issues.failure_explanation: The proof of Theorem \ref{theorem4.2} closes the chain of inequalities by inserting the L^2-interpolation estimate \eqref{eqn:lemma4-3}, which is stated and cited under the hypothesis $\Eb \in \Hb^{s+1}(\Omega)$. The theorem assumes only $\Eb \in \Hb^{s+1/2}(\Omega)$ with $\nabla\times\Eb \in \Hb^s$, so \eqref{eqn:lemma4-3} is applied outside its hypotheses. With only $\Eb \in \Hb^{s+1/2}$, the applicable L^2 bound is $\|\Eb-\Pib_N\Eb\|_0 \le C h^{\min\{s-1/2,\,l\}+1}$, so the terms $(C_{Eb}+C_{Ehb})\|\Eb-\Eb_I\|_{0,\Omega}$ and $(1+1/\varepsilon)m\|\Eb-\Eb_I\|^2_{0,\Omega}$ in \eqref{eqn:error bound} scale only like $h^{\min\{s-1/2,\,l\}+1}$ and $h^{2(\min\{s-1/2,l\}+1)}$; combined with the $h^{2\min\{s,l\}}$ terms from $T_1$ and $r_h$, the argument yields at best the rate $\tfrac12\min\{\min\{s-1/2,l\}+1,\,2\min\{s,l\}\}$, which is strictly weaker than the claimed $h^{(\min\{s,l\}+1)/2}$ whenever $s < l+1/2$. In particular, for the advertised case $l=1$, $\Eb\in\Hb^{3/2}$, $\nabla\times\Eb\in\Hb^1$, the argument gives only $\|\Eb-\Eb_h\|_h \lesssim h^{3/4}$, not the stated $\|\Eb-\Eb_h\|_h\le Ch$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen the hypothesis to $\Eb \in \Hb^{\min\{s,l\}+1}(\Omega)$ (e.g. $\Eb \in \Hb^2(\Omega)$ for $l=1$), under which the displayed chain does deliver the claimed rate; or rework the treatment of the hemivariational (Clarke) terms to recover the claimed rate under the stated hypotheses.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's central a priori error estimate \eqref{error_bd} is not established under its stated hypotheses; in particular the claim following the theorem that linear elements ($l=1$) achieve the optimal order $\|\Eb-\Eb_h\|_h \le C h$ under $\Eb\in\Hb^{3/2}$, $\nabla\times\Eb\in\Hb^1$ is unsupported, and the abstract/introductory/numerical prose claims of 'optimal convergence order' inherit this gap.
issues.title: A priori error estimate not established under stated regularity
issues.why_classification: A contained repair exists (strengthen one hypothesis, or a contained nontrivial reestimate of the two $L^2$-consistency terms) and a comparable a priori estimate with the same optimal-order conclusion under slightly stronger regularity survives; no new global proof architecture is required, but the advertised regularity regime for the stated rate is not supported as written.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the justification '$\llbracket\nabla\times\Eb\rrbracket = \zerob$' by the Maxwell interface condition that the tangential trace of $\mu^{-1}\nabla\times\Eb$ is continuous across interior faces (which holds for the exact solution) in both the consistency proof and the proof of Theorem \ref{theorem4.2}.
issues.overall_effect: The consistency proof (Theorem \ref{thm:added-1}) and the corresponding step in the proof of Theorem \ref{theorem4.2} rest on an unestablished premise whenever $\mu$ is discontinuous across material interfaces; the final conclusions remain correct once the Maxwell interface condition (tangential continuity of $\mu^{-1}\nabla\times\Eb$) is supplied, but as written the step is unjustified.
issues.title: Interior-jump term discarded on an unjustified premise
issues.why_classification: A short, local premise repair (cite the standard interface condition instead of the curl-jump fact) preserves the consistency conclusion and every dependent claim, with no new argument needed.
